title: Hunt it on the box
briefing: The log you pulled mentioned a suspicious child process on web-01, and the
box is pinned at 100% CPU. Something root-owned is hiding in /tmp.
Log into web-01, find the rogue process, and kill it. It runs as root, so
you'll need sudo to stop it.
tips: On web-01: `ps aux` and look for the CPU hog running from /tmp.
It's root-owned — `sudo kill <PID>` to stop it. Confirm it's gone with ps again.
objective: SSH into web-01 and kill the rogue root-owned process (the CPU hog running from /tmp) so it's no longer running.
expert_objective: Something root-owned is melting web-01. Log in and end it.
hints: Get on the box and find it: `ssh admin@web-01`, then `ps aux`. The hog is /tmp/.x/kworkerd at ~96% CPU (PID 6931).
It's root's process, so stop it with privilege: `sudo kill 6931`.
`ssh admin@web-01`, `ps aux`, then `sudo kill 6931`. `ps aux` again shows it gone.
solution:
ssh admin@web-01
ps aux
sudo kill 6931
explanation: Incident response over ssh: get on the affected host, find the offender with ps, and stop it — with sudo, because it's not your process. You just handled a compromise on a server across the network, using only the shell.
